skills.name: Energy: types, uses and energy values

note.text:
Energy is the ability to do work. The body gets chemical energy from food and turns it into heat (to keep warm) and movement (muscles), and uses it for growth and for the work of the organs (heartbeat, breathing).
Basal metabolism is the energy used at complete rest just to stay alive. Active people, growing children and pregnant women need more energy.
Food energy is measured in kilocalories (kcal) or kilojoules (kJ); 1 kcal is about 4.2 kJ.
Energy values of the macronutrients (per gram):
• carbohydrate: 4 kcal (17 kJ)   • protein: 4 kcal (17 kJ)   • fat: 9 kcal (37 kJ).
Example: a snack with 20 g carbohydrate, 5 g protein and 10 g fat gives 20 × 4 + 5 × 4 + 10 × 9 = 80 + 20 + 90 = 190 kcal.

worked_example.problem: A plate of food contains {c} g carbohydrate, {p} g protein and {f} g fat. How many kilocalories does it give?
steps: Total: {c * four} + {p * four} + {f * nine} = {c * four + p * four + f * nine} kcal.
worked_example.answer: {c * four + p * four + f * nine} kcal
checks: c * four + p * four + f * nine == 232

cards.idea: The body uses food energy for heat, movement, growth and the work of its organs.
example: Basal metabolism: energy used at rest just to stay alive.

cards.idea: One gram of carbohydrate or protein gives {four} kcal; one gram of fat gives {nine} kcal.
To find the energy of a food, multiply each nutrient's grams by its value and add.
example: {c} g carbohydrate + {f} g fat: {c} × {four} + {f} × {nine} = {c * four + f * nine} kcal.

check.prompt: A meal contains {c} g carbohydrate, {p} g protein and {f} g fat. How many kilocalories does it give?

misconceptions.explain: Fat gives {nine} kcal per gram, not {four}.
That is the mass in grams; multiply each by its energy value.

solution: Carbohydrate: {c} × {four} = {c * 4} kcal; protein: {p} × {four} = {p * 4} kcal; fat: {f} × {nine} = {f * 9} kcal.

pick.r: the energy used at rest just to stay alive
pick.y: Basal metabolism keeps the heart, breathing and organs working at rest.

pick.r: a farmer doing heavy work all day
pick.y: Heavy physical work needs the most energy.
